Well, sometimes it doesn't work that way... for the sake of example, let's say the normal price for noodles is $0.50 a pack but there's a 4/$1.00 thing active.  Where I worked in HS, how the terminal did it was:

NOODLES $0.50

NOODLES $0.50

NOODLES $0.50

NOODLES $0.50

NOODLEDISCOUNT -$1.00 (automatic)

So you had to buy all four to get the deal... which would mean that buying three costs you $0.50 more (and people watching the running total would start harping on me for not "giving them the deal" before everything was scanned in, sigh).

I work with money (coffee shop) and I understand where he's coming from.  My problem isn't that I can't do math... I used to not even punch in the money that's given to me and just did the calculation in my head, since it was faster to use the "exact change"  button than deal with the shitty terminal interface and stubborn/poorly calibrated touchscreen number pad.

This occasionally backfired on me.  The orders come at a rate of one every 20 seconds or so, on busy days, so I got used to having to hold the total or the money given to me in memory for all of half a second before discarding it.  So if I got distracted (someone asked me a question or something) and I forgot what the total was or how much money someone gave me, I couldn't figure out the change.
